title: Closed points of a product
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over a field $K$ and
$z\in X\times_KY$ with images $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$. Then $z$
is a closed point of $X\times_KY$ if and only if $x$ and $y$ are
closed points.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Jacobson-space, finite-morphism, pullback, and discrete-fibre lemmas. The forward implication follows from closePoints_subset_preimage_closedPoints. For the converse, pull back the closed-point immersion of the first projection point. Its composite with the structure morphism is finite by the Jacobson finite-type criterion, hence the induced map q to Y is finite and has discrete fibres. The chosen product point is in the image of the second projection j of this pullback. The fibre over the closed second projection point is discrete, and its singleton is closed because that point is closed. The closed immersion j maps this singleton to the original point, proving it is closed.
